summary: A fourth-century collection of monastic homilies and question-and-answer sessions. Homily VIII describes what happens to people at prayer: the 'sign of the cross' appearing in light and fastening itself on the inward man, a garment flashing with light, and 'the light shining in the heart' disclosing a deeper hidden light, after which grace withdraws and a 'foggy power' veils the still-burning lamp. The speaker says he has himself 'in part come to that measure' and denies that it makes a man perfect. Other homilies treat the soul becoming 'all light, all eye' and the light that will one day show on the body. Practice context is unceasing prayer and waiting on grace; no technique for producing the light is given, and the fluctuation is ascribed to grace's management.
why_relevant: Early first-person report of light seen during prayer with a statement of what the person was doing and an explicit account of the light dimming and returning; it is the background that later hesychast writers cite.
